previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and chest pain after being found crawling on the ground due to respiratory distress. He had recently left two prior hospitals against medical advice. Evaluation revealed multifocal pneumonia and acute exacerbation of COPD, with evidence of acute on chronic systolic heart failure and mild acute kidney injury. He was treated with levofloxacin, steroids, bronchodilators, and diuresis. An echocardiogram confirmed severe left ventricular dysfunction. He had a brief asymptomatic run of ventricular tachycardia. Despite efforts to arrange methadone treatment, no immediate placement was available. The patient understood the risks but chose to leave against medical advice to attend a future methadone clinic appointment, expressing a desire to become sober. He was discharged on antibiotics, heart failure medications, and supportive prescriptions with close follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with history of COPD, recent 
multifocal PNA s/p 7day course of levofloxacin, A. Fib, sCHF, 
and CAD who presents with palpitations and shortness of breath 
likely due to combination of COPD exacerbation, A. Fib with RVR, 
and decompensated heart failure 

ACTIVE DIAGNOSES:

# Systolic, decompensated heart failure: Patient initially 
appeared dry but showed signs of volume overload on HD#2.  He 
was given lasix for  days (w/ net -1.5L-2L daily) and shortness 
of breath improved.  Patient was also tachycardic in low 100s on 
telemetry and was given metoprolol 75mg TID and diltiazem but 
transitioned to metoprolol 100mg TID and lisinopril 5mg.  HR was 
stable in the ___ on metoprolol 100mg TID so the patient was 
discharged on metoprolol XL 300mg once daily. 

# COPD Exacerbation: Patient's symptoms improved w/ steroid and 
ipratropium. Patient completed a 6day course of PO prednisone 
and was restarted on albuterol when tachycardia was resolved.  
At time of discharge, patient able to ambulate w/o respiratory 
distress nor ambulatory desats. He will be switched from Advair 
to fluticasone daily to avoid the beta-adrenergic component of 
Advair (given his atrial fibrillation and tendency to become 
tachycardic without high dose beta-blockers). He should continue 
taking Spiriva daily. He was instructed to limit PRN albuterol 
use due to tachycardia with albuterol nebs in the hospital.

# Heroin withdrawal: Patient has a history of daily heroin use 
(last used ___ ___. Pt was genuinely interested in getting 
clean. Patient was given daily 40mg methadone during his 
hospital course and showed minimal signs of withdrawal.  Patient 
will be transferred to ___ ___.  He will also go to 
Addiction Treatment ___ the following day 
(___) to be evaluated to join the ___ clinic.   

# Multifocal pneumonia: Patient completed a 7-day course 
levofloxacin on ___ and showed no sign of PNA clinically, 
although CXR showed opacities in R lung concerning for 
recurrent/aspiration PNA.   Patient will need a follow up CXR in 
8 wks to document resolution of infiltrates 

# Atrial fibrillation with RVR: patient's CHADS2 score is 1 
(sCHF). A discussion regarding anticoagulation risk/benefits 
should be held as outpatient. The patient did have tachycardia 
early on in his hospital stay. His beta blocker was uptitrated 
to a dose of 100mg Q8h with good rate control at that dose. He 
will be discharged on metoprolol XL 300mg daily for rate 
control. 

# NSVT ___ dilated cardiomyopathy: During patient's prior 
admission, he was noted to have several episodes of NSVT (8 to 
25 beat runs). He was asymptomatic with these episodes. The 
patient has a follow up appointment with cardiology to discuss 
possibility of ICD placement once he demonstrates adherence and 
stays clean from IVDU. He should continue on beta blocker.

# ___. Cr 1.3 on admission, baseline 0.8. Likely pre-renal, 
since it trended down after receiving 500cc NS. The patient's 
diuretic and ACEi were held for a day and restarted when Cr 
returned to baseline. Cr on discharge was 0.9.

DES to
